outcome: percent of multinucleation of Interstitial Trophoblasts (ITs)
cohort: The study included 20 women who underwent gravid hysterectomies due to placenta creta between 2006 and 2012.
finding: Uterine damage caused by Cesarean sections is associated with poor decidualization, abnormal trophoblastic invasion, incomplete vascular remodeling, fewer multinuclei trophoblasts, and deep infiltrative pathology.
mod_finding: A history of Cesarean Section (CS) was present in 80% of patients, and all cases with placenta percreta (N=10) had undergone more than two previous CSs, linking prior CSs to more severe forms of placenta creta.
